question: Which main immune cells does HIV target and attack inside the body?
explanation: You've got this! HIV zeroes in on CD4+ T-lymphocytes because these are the cells that normally coordinate our body's defense against infections. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h1)

question: Why does HIV rely on the enzyme reverse transcriptase once it enters a host cell?

options.A: To cut open the host cell membrane
options.B: To repair damaged viral genetic material
options.C: To destroy competing white blood cells
options.D: To convert viral RNA into DNA

explanation: Think of reverse transcriptase as a translator. It changes the virus's RNA into DNA so the instructions can blend right into the host cell's own chromosomes! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h1)

question: A patient's CD4 count drops to what level to officially mark the transition from HIV to AIDS?
explanation: Keep this number handy for the wards: when the CD4 count falls below 200 cells per microliter, the condition is classified as AIDS. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h2)

question: What happens to the amount of virus (viral load) during the long, quiet chronic latency stage of HIV?

options.A: It drops to lower levels compared to the acute stage
options.B: It increases rapidly every single day
options.C: It remains exactly identical to the acute stage peak
options.D: It disappears completely from the bloodstream

explanation: Great job! During latency, the viral load settles down compared to the massive spike during early infection, though the virus is still quietly active. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h2)

question: Which germ is the most common culprit behind fungal pneumonia in patients with advanced HIV?
explanation: Spot on! Pneumocystis jirovecii loves to strike when the immune system is deeply weakened, causing a serious type of pneumonia. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h3)

question: An advanced HIV patient comes in with distinct purplish skin lesions and ongoing watery diarrhea. What are those skin spots called?
explanation: You're doing great. Those telltale purplish or brownish skin lesions are known as Kaposi sarcoma, a cancer linked to HIV. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h3)

question: Besides antibodies, what specific viral marker do fourth-generation HIV tests look for?
explanation: Awesome work! Fourth-gen tests search for the p24 antigen alongside antibodies, helping us catch recent infections much earlier. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h4)

question: Why must a positive rapid HIV screening test always be backed up by a confirmatory test?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of the patient
options.B: To rule out false positive results and confirm the diagnosis
options.C: To check if the patient has received past vaccinations
options.D: To determine which specific medication the patient prefers

explanation: Screening tests are sensitive, but they can occasionally give false alarms. A confirmatory test guarantees absolute accuracy before starting lifelong treatment. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h4)

question: What exactly does a plasma viral load test measure in an HIV patient?

options.A: The concentration of antibodies in the saliva
options.B: The total number of healthy white blood cells
options.C: The amount of circulating viral RNA in the blood
options.D: The percentage of red blood cells destroyed by the virus

explanation: Think of viral load as a count of active virus copies floating around in a milliliter of plasma. It tells us how fast the virus is multiplying! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h5)

question: Why do nurses track CD4 T-cell counts regularly during antiretroviral therapy?

options.A: To evaluate the recovery and strength of the immune system
options.B: To predict how much weight the patient will gain
options.C: To decide if the patient needs immediate blood transfusions
options.D: To calculate the exact date the patient was infected

explanation: You've got this! Tracking CD4 counts is like checking the health score of the immune system to see how well it's bouncing back. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h5)

question: Why is checking nutritional status such an important part of nursing care for HIV patients?

options.A: Vitamins are the only treatment needed for early-stage disease
options.B: Poor nutrition prevents the skin from absorbing medications
options.C: Dietary changes can completely cure the viral infection
options.D: Wasting syndrome and chronic diarrhea frequently threaten recovery

explanation: Spot on. Good nutrition keeps the immune system strong, while complications like wasting and diarrhea can quickly pull a patient down. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h6)

question: A newly diagnosed patient is terrified and refuses to talk about medication schedules. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Report the patient immediately to local public health authorities
options.B: Withhold all educational materials until the patient asks for them
options.C: Force the patient to swallow the first dose of pills right away
options.D: Provide empathetic, non-judgmental support and address emotional distress

explanation: Empathy first! Building trust and helping patients work through their fear and stigma is always the essential first step before teaching them about medications. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h6)
